bug_description.original: A vulnerability exists where the mask is not set to 0 for directories, which can lead to buffer overflows due to incorrect truncation of the window.
bug_description.normalized: The staged 109-byte RAR5 witness starts directly with a FILE header whose `file_flags` mark the entry as a directory but whose `header_flags` still advertise 64 bytes of compressed data. `process_head_file()` therefore sets `rar->cstate.window_size = 0` while also selecting the compressed `FASTEST` method. `init_unpack()` then unconditionally computes `rar->cstate.window_mask = rar->cstate.window_size - 1`, turning the mask into all ones, and allocates `window_buf` with `calloc(1, 0)`, which AddressSanitizer reports as a 1-byte region. The first compressed block header (`44 2f 31`) advertises no Huffman table, so the freshly zeroed literal decode table stays all-zero and `decode_number()` yields literal `0`. The first literal write lands at `window_buf[0]`, then the next loop test in `do_uncompress_block()` hits `write_ptr - last_write_ptr > (window_size >> 1)` (1 > 0) before the block-finished check, so `block_parsing_finished` stays 0 and `process_block()` leaves the same `block_buf` cached for later resumption. `do_uncompress_file()` publishes that one byte, a later `rar5_read_data()` call drains it through `use_data()`, and the following call re-enters `process_block()` on the cached block via `else { p = rar->cstate.block_buf; }`. The next literal store then writes `window_buf[1]`, triggering the observed 1-byte heap-buffer-overflow. The fix guards the mask assignment so zero-sized directory windows keep `window_mask = 0`.

source.description: First project-side read inside the RAR5 FILE-header parser that materializes the staged entry's compressed-data extent.
source.value_from: In the staged 109-byte witness, the first base block after the RAR5 signature is a FILE header (`header_id == 0x02`, `header_flags == 0x02`). At byte offset 15 this read decodes `data_size = 0x40` (64), and line 1312 stores that exact count in `rar->file.bytes_remaining` for the compressed stream later parsed by `process_block()`.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. On the resumed literal-write path, `write_idx` is 1 and `cmask` is all ones, so the store targets `window_buf[1]`, one byte past the 1-byte allocation returned by `calloc(1, 0)`.
sink.note: The saved trace reports `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 1` at `archive_read_support_format_rar5.c:2424:55`, on address `0x602000000051`, exactly 0 bytes to the right of the 1-byte region allocated at line 1834.

root_cause.description: Root cause: `init_unpack()` subtracts 1 from a zero directory `window_size`, turning the circular-window mask into all ones instead of a safe zero mask.
root_cause.note: The staged fixing patch wraps this assignment in `if (rar->cstate.window_size) ... else rar->cstate.window_mask = 0;`, so directory entries no longer get an all-ones mask.

parser_admitted.description: The first base block after the RAR5 signature decodes as `HEAD_FILE` with `header_flags == HFL_DATA`, so parsing is admitted directly into the FILE-header handler that reads the directory bit, compression fields, and compressed-data size used on the crashing path.

tainted_value_origin.description: The exact vulnerable parser state is created here: the PoC's directory bit and `compression_info` field combine to produce a zero unpack window while still selecting the compressed-data path.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: In the staged header, line 1330 reads `file_flags = 0x01`, so `is_dir` becomes true at line 1342. Line 1357 then reads bytes `ff 01` as `compression_info = 0x00ff`, yielding `c_method == FASTEST` and forcing `rar->cstate.window_size = 0` at line 1363.

coarse_trace.summary: The staged archive's first base block is parsed directly as a FILE header with data, admitting execution into `process_head_file()`.
The FILE header materializes 64 bytes of compressed data and attacker-controlled directory/compression fields that set `window_size = 0` and `method = FASTEST`.

The decompressor initializes a zero-sized window by allocating `window_buf` with `calloc(1, 0)` but still setting `window_mask = window_size - 1`, leaving an all-ones index mask over a 1-byte allocation.

The first compressed block header advertises no Huffman tables, so the zeroed literal table remains active; one literal byte is written to `window_buf[0]`, then the next loop iteration exits via the zero-window throttle before `block_parsing_finished` can be set.

`do_uncompress_file()` queues `[0, 1)` and advances `last_write_ptr` to 1; after libarchive drains that byte, the next `rar5_read_data()` call finds no queued output and `process_block()` resumes the cached `block_buf` through its `else` branch.
The resumed literal path runs with `write_ptr == last_write_ptr == 1` and the all-ones mask still active, so the next store writes `window_buf[1]` past the 1-byte allocation.

fine_trace.note: The first base block after the RAR5 signature decodes as `header_id == HEAD_FILE` with `header_flags == HFL_DATA`, so parsing enters the FILE-header handler instead of `HEAD_MAIN` or `HEAD_SERVICE`. The staged witness does not contain a preceding MAIN header.

Reads the FILE header's data-size varint. In the staged bytes this value is `0x40`, so the entry carries 64 bytes of compressed data and line 1312 stores that exact count in `rar->file.bytes_remaining`.
Reads the FILE flags varint as `0x01`; `file_flags & DIRECTORY` therefore makes `is_dir` nonzero at line 1342. This attacker-controlled directory bit is what later forces a zero unpack window.

The staged bytes `ff 01` decode to `compression_info = 0x00ff`. That yields `c_method == FASTEST` and, because step 3 made `is_dir` true, line 1363 sets `rar->cstate.window_size = 0` instead of a normal dictionary. The same FILE header already provided `unpacked_size = 32` at line 1333/1443.

Because step 4 set `rar->cstate.method` to `FASTEST`, `do_unpack()` takes the decompression path rather than `do_unstore_file()`. That is what reaches `init_unpack()` and `do_uncompress_block()` for this directory entry.

Root cause. `init_unpack()` runs with `rar->cstate.window_size == 0`, so subtracting 1 produces an all-ones mask (`SIZE_MAX`, later `cmask == -1`) instead of a safe zero mask for directories. The fix adds the missing zero-size guard here.
With `window_size == 0`, `calloc(1, 0)` creates the heap object that ASan later reports as a 1-byte region `[ptr, ptr + 1)`. This allocation is the storage that the resumed literal write overruns.

The same initialization starts decompression at the beginning of the zero-sized window and clears the literal decode table. Unless a later block advertises new Huffman tables, `decode_number()` will operate on this all-zero table state.

The first compressed-block header comes from bytes `44 2f 31`. `parse_block_header()` decodes `block_flags_u8 = 0x44`, `block_cksum = 0x2f`, and a 1-byte `block_size = 49`; after the 3-byte header is consumed, `cur_block_size` is 49 and `block_buf` aliases the attacker-controlled block payload. Because `rar->last_block_hdr.block_flags.is_table_present == 0`, line 2824 skips `parse_tables()`, so the zeroed literal table from step 8 remains in force.

With no tables present and `rar->cstate.ld` all zero, the first `decode_number()` falls through to `table->decode_num[0]` and returns `num = 0`. The literal branch is therefore taken, `write_idx` is 0 because the pointers were reset in step 8, and the first byte write lands at `window_buf[0]`, the only in-bounds byte of the allocation. `write_ptr` advances to 1.

After step 10 stores the first literal, the same `while(1)` loop iterates again with `write_ptr == 1` and `last_write_ptr == 0`. Because `window_size >> 1` is 0, the throttle guard at lines 2379-2386 is true and breaks immediately. That break happens before the block-finished guard at lines 2389-2395, so `block_parsing_finished` stays 0 and `process_block()` does not consume or replace the current block state.

No filters are pending, so `max_end_pos` is `rar->cstate.write_ptr == 1`. Because `last_write_ptr` is still 0, the equality test at line 3056 is false and the `else` arm executes. `push_window_data()` queues one ready-data record for `[0, 1)`, and line 3071 leaves `last_write_ptr` at 1.

On the next `rar5_read_data()` entry after step 12, `use_data()` finds the queued ready-data slot, returns its single-byte buffer/size/offset to the caller, and clears `d->used` to 0. That drains the only published byte.

On the following `rar5_read_data()` call, step 13 has already cleared the only ready-data slot, so `use_data()` falls through to `do_unpack()`. Because step 11 left `block_parsing_finished == 0`, `process_block()` takes the `else` arm at line 2833 and reuses `rar->cstate.block_buf` instead of parsing a new compressed-block header. Decompression therefore resumes on the same partially decoded 49-byte block.

On the resumed `do_uncompress_block()` call, the throttle test at lines 2379-2386 is now false because `write_ptr - last_write_ptr == 0` and `window_size >> 1 == 0`, so execution reaches another literal decode. The same zero-table decode yields `num = 0`; now `write_idx` is 1, and with root-cause mask `cmask == -1`, `write_idx & cmask` stays 1. This store writes `window_buf[1]`, which ASan reports as address `0x602000000051`, exactly one byte past the 1-byte allocation from step 7.

poc.trigger: The staged `poc` is a 109-byte raw RAR5 archive. `archive_read_next_header()` returns its lone FILE entry, and repeated `archive_read_data()` calls on that entry reproduce the saved AddressSanitizer heap-buffer-overflow in `do_uncompress_block()`.

format.name: 109-byte RAR5 FILE header for a directory entry with compressed data
format.contract: The witness begins with the RAR5 signature `52 61 72 21 1a 07 01 00`. Its first and only base block is a FILE header whose parsed fields are `header_id = 0x02`, `header_flags = 0x02 (HFL_DATA)`, `data_size = 64`, `file_flags = 0x01 (DIRECTORY)`, `unpacked_size = 32`, `file_attr = 32`, `compression_info = 0x00ff`, `host_os = 0`, and `name_size = 30`. The file data begins at offset 53 with compressed-block header bytes `44 2f 31`, which `parse_block_header()` accepts as `block_flags_u8 = 0x44`, `block_cksum = 0x2f`, and a one-byte `block_size = 49` with no new Huffman tables. These exact staged values are sufficient to reproduce the saved ASan heap-buffer-overflow.
